translationRepairs: Now you campaign against the southern Yi, have Yelang come to court, reduce the Qiang and Bo, seize Zhuya, build cities and towns, penetrate deep into the Xiongnu, and burn their Dragon City—discussers praise it.

Now you campaign against the southern Yi, have Yelang come to court, reduce the Qiang and Bo, seize Huizhou, build cities and towns, penetrate deep into the Xiongnu, and burn their Dragon City—discussers praise it.
Focus unit has 略薉州, not 珠崖; Zhuya is the wrong place, and Huizhou correctly renders 薉州.
yiyin day sweated over the kitchen cauldrons, the Grand Duke Tai peddled from a butcher's block, Baili Xi sold himself into service, Ning Qi sang beside his ox—all to escape that plight.
Yi Yin labored over pots and chopping boards; the Grand Duke was reduced to working as a butcher; Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen. In this way they escaped their hardships.
伊尹 is Yi Yin, while the full revision also renders 鼎俎, 鼓刀, and the four men's emergence from hardship in natural English.
Therefore yiyin day toiled at cauldrons and stands, Grand Duke Tai was trapped at drumming the knife, Baili sold himself, Ningzi fed oxen—leaving this misfortune.
Thus Yi Yin labored at cauldrons and chopping boards, the Grand Duke was reduced to wielding a butcher's knife, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen; thereby they escaped these hardships.
伊尹 is Yi Yin; the fuller revision removes the corrupt name and gives each allusion and the concluding clause a grammatical rendering.

When the realm is at peace and the throne is wise, great men come unbidden, as when Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu won the service of Hou Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, yiyin day, and Lü Wang—radiant ministers ranked in solemn order, pooling their insight until ruler and subject shine the brighter together.

Thus, in an age of peace under a sage ruler, outstanding elders come of their own accord. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu obtained the service of Hou Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Lü Wang. Brilliant at court and solemn in their ranks, they joined their finest insights and magnified the glory of ruler and minister alike.
The source names Yi Yin and describes worthy ministers gathering naturally around sage rulers; the revision restores the name and makes the full comparison readable.

Therefore when the age is peaceful and the lord is sage, outstanding elders will arrive of themselves; like the lords Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, obtaining Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, yiyin day, and Lü Wang—bright bright in court, solemn solemn arrayed in rows, gathering essence, meeting spirit, mutually obtaining increased splendor.

Therefore, when the age is peaceful and the ruler is a sage, outstanding elders arrive of themselves. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu obtained Hou Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Lü Wang. Brilliant at court and solemnly arrayed, they united their finest insight and spirit, bringing greater splendor to ruler and minister alike.
The literal must restore Yi Yin and preserve the sentence's parallel list, courtly imagery, and conclusion in grammatical English.
Critics dismissed such verse as frivolous and beside the point of government, but the emperor replied, 'Confucius himself asked whether a game of chess was not still better than doing nothing at all.
Critics dismissed such verse as frivolous and irrelevant, but the emperor replied with a line from the Analects: 'Are there not board games? Playing them is still better than doing nothing.'
The emperor quotes the Analects without naming Confucius directly; identifying the work preserves useful context while rendering 博弈 as board games rather than chess alone.

Yet their land south did not pass Min-Yue, north did not pass Taiyuan, yet the realm collapsed and rebelled; disaster finally at the end of the Second Generation; the song of the Great Wall to this day has not ceased.

Yet Qin's territory extended no farther south than Minyue and no farther north than Taiyuan, and still the realm disintegrated in revolt. Disaster finally came at the end of the Second Emperor's reign, and songs of the Great Wall have not ceased to this day.
In this Qin context 二世 is the Second Emperor; the full revision also restores the sentence's subject and contrast rather than changing one phrase inside an ungrammatical draft.
Xing said: 'The county official once said Xing is superior to Minister Xue—I am easy to help.
Yang Xing said, 'The emperor once said that I was better than Grandee Xue. It should be easy for you to help me.
Here 縣官 means the emperor, and 我易助也 means that Yang Xing should be easy for Jia Juanzhi to help; it does not describe Xing as an ally.
If you want preferment, brother, follow my advice: humor him for now, and you will win your way in.'
If you want to advance, just follow my advice: accommodate Shi Xian for now, and you will gain access to the court.'
弟 is the adverb 'just,' not kinship; 合意 means temporarily accommodating Shi Xian's wishes, not merely humoring an unnamed person.
Now if you wish to advance, younger brother follow my plan; for the moment join his intent, then you will be able to enter.'
Now, if you wish to advance, just follow my plan: align yourself with Shi Xian for the moment, and you will be able to enter the court.'
弟 is the adverb 'just,' not 'younger brother'; the revision makes the implied object Shi Xian and the goal of court access explicit from context.

s0001’s title 嚴朱吾丘主父徐嚴終王賈傳 lists only surnames; the first 嚴 is Yan Zhu (嚴助) and the second 嚴 is Yan An (嚴安), while 賈 is Jia Juanzhi (賈捐之). The before invents Yan Cang and Jia Yi; the proposed after wrongly makes both 嚴 into Yan An.
Now wild beasts share horns—brightness is the same root.
Now wild beasts share a joined horn—clearly showing they are of the same root.
In 今野獸并角，明同本也, 明 is adverbial “clearly,” not “brightness,” and 并角 is a joined horn; the proposed literal corrects both misreadings.
When six wild geese beat their way upwind, the Spring and Autumn Annals read it as ill omen.
When six wild geese beat their way upwind, it is read as a contrary omen.
s0077 蓋六鶂退飛，逆也 names no book; inventing the Spring and Autumn Annals is unsupported. The proposed slash “contrary/ill” is unnatural, so the wording is tightened while keeping 逆.

Hand that smith the rough ingot of a Gan Jiang blade, let him quench the edge in pure water and true the guard on a Yue whetstone, and the finished sword will slice dragons in the river and rhinoceros hide on land as easily as a comet streaks or a brush draws a line in wet plaster.

Have a skilled smith cast the rough blank of a Gan Jiang blade, quench its edge in pure water and true its guard on a Yue whetstone, and the finished sword will slice dragons in the river and rhinoceros hide on land as easily as a comet streaks or a brush draws a line in wet plaster.
s0153 巧冶鑄干將之樸 needs a grammatical English opening for the skilled smith casting the Gan Jiang blank; “Hand that smith” is ungrammatical and the proposed repair restores the sense.
Yi Yin labored over pots and chopping boards; the Grand Duke was reduced to working as a butcher; Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen. In this way they escaped their hardships.
Yi Yin labored over pots and chopping boards; the Grand Duke was reduced to working as a butcher; Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen. In this way they suffered these hardships.
In 離此患也, 離 is 罹 “suffer/encounter”; the preceding hardships are what the worthies underwent, not what they escaped, and the replacement is accurate.
Thus Yi Yin labored at cauldrons and chopping boards, the Grand Duke was reduced to wielding a butcher's knife, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen; thereby they escaped these hardships.
Thus Yi Yin labored at cauldrons and chopping boards, the Grand Duke was reduced to wielding a butcher's knife, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen; thereby they suffered these hardships.
The same 離此患也 on the literal line means suffer these hardships, not escape them; the proposed fix is correct.
If obtaining intent is thus, then what barbarian prohibition does not stop, what command does not go?
If obtaining intent is thus, then what prohibition does not stop, what command does not go?
In 則胡禁不止，曷令不行, 胡 is interrogative in parallel with 曷, not the ethnonym “barbarian”; removing that gloss is required.

Following and roaming the tendency of nature, in the field of quiet plain non-action, auspicious signs arrive of themselves, long life has no border, harmonious ease with folded hands, forever ten thousand years—why must one bend and stretch and twist trust like Pengzu, exhale and inhale like Qiao and Song, subtly cut off custom and leave the world!

Following and roaming the tendency of nature, in the field of quiet plain non-action, auspicious signs arrive of themselves, long life has no border, harmonious ease with folded hands, forever ten thousand years—why must one bend and stretch like Pengzu, exhale and inhale like Qiao and Song, subtly cut off custom and leave the world!
詘信 is the binome 屈伸 “bend and stretch”; reading 信 as “trust” is a semantic error, and the proposed deletion fixes it.

The emperor ordered Bao and Zhang Ziqiao and others together to await edict; repeatedly followed Bao and others on release hunts; at favored palaces and lodges, then composed songs and eulogies, ranked their high and low, and by gradation granted silk.

The emperor ordered Bao and Zhang Ziqiao and others together to await edict; repeatedly took Bao and others along on hunts; at favored palaces and lodges, then composed songs and eulogies, ranked their high and low, and by gradation granted silk.
數從褒等放獵 has the emperor take Bao and the others along on hunts; “followed Bao” reverses the accompaniment relation expressed by 從.
In decline, kings marched south and never came home; Duke Huan of Qi had to rescue the house of Zhou, and Confucius set the record straight in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
In decline, kings marched south and never came home; Duke Huan of Qi had to rescue the house of Zhou, and Confucius fixed its text.
s0221 has only 孔子定其文; the idiomatic’s “Spring and Autumn Annals” is an unsupported addition, and “fixed its text” matches the Chinese.
Yang Xing said, 'The emperor once said that I was better than Grandee Xue. It should be easy for you to help me.
Xing said: 'The emperor once said Xing was better than Grandee Xue; I am easy to help.

s0268 興曰：「縣官嘗言興瘉薛大夫，我易助也」 uses Xing (not “I”) as the compared person and ends “I am easy to help.” The before errs on both points; the proposed “county office [His Majesty]” is an awkward calque—縣官 here is the emperor.
Your servant foolishly thinks that what are not cap-and-girdle states, what the Tribute of Yu reaches, what the Spring and Autumn governs—all may for the moment be left undone.

Your servant foolishly thinks that those that are not cap-and-girdle states, that the Tribute of Yu does not reach, and that the Spring and Autumn does not govern, may for the moment all be left alone.

非 scopes over 冠帶之國、禹貢所及、春秋所治: lands outside the cap-and-girdle realm and outside Yu Gong / Spring and Autumn geography. The before treats the last two as positive categories to abandon; the proposed after wrongly keeps them inside the civilized sphere.

Thereupon an edict was issued, saying: 'Zhuya captives killed clerks and people, turned their backs and rebelled as traitors; now those who court discuss say some may strike, some may guard, some wish to abandon them—their aims each differ.

Thereupon an edict was issued, saying: 'Zhuya's rebels killed clerks and people, turned their backs and rebelled as traitors; now those discussing at court say some may strike, some may guard, some wish to abandon them—their aims each differ.
珠崖虜殺吏民 means Zhuya’s rebels/caitiffs killed officials and people, and 廷議者 are those discussing at court; “captives” and “those who court discuss” are mistranslations.
Even ancestral offerings are curtailed in years of famine; how can I court the shame of chasing a pointless slight to the ends of the earth?
Even ancestral-temple sacrifices are incomplete in famine years; how much more should one avoid a humiliation that is not truly shameful?

況乎辟不嫌之辱哉 follows the famine-sacrifice a fortiori: 辟 is avoid/set aside, and 不嫌之辱 is a disgrace that is not real shame. The before invents “chasing a pointless slight”; the proposed “how much less should I shrink from” garbles 況乎 and 辟.
The document says: "Slanderous talk and extinguished conduct alarm Our hosts."
The Documents say: "Slanderous talk and extinguished conduct alarm Our hosts."
書曰 is the standard citation formula for the Documents (Shangshu); singular “document” understates that titled classic, and the idiomatic already reads “Documents.”

The world calls Gongsun Hong having excluded Zhufu, Zhang Tang having trapped Yan Zhu, Shi Xian having slandered Juanzhi; inspecting their tracks and conduct, Zhufu sought the eminence of the minister's tripod and obtained clan execution; Yan and Jia passed in and out of the forbidden gate summoning power and profit—their deaths were each their proper lot—what resentment then about exclusion and entrapment!

The world says Gongsun Hong excluded Zhufu, Zhang Tang trapped Yan Zhu, and Shi Xian slandered Juanzhi; inspecting their tracks and conduct, Zhufu sought the eminence of the minister's tripod and obtained clan execution; Yan and Jia passed in and out of the forbidden gate summoning power and profit—their deaths were each their proper lot—what resentment then about exclusion and entrapment!
世稱公孫弘排主父，張湯陷嚴助，石顯譖捐之 needs finite verbs; “calls Gongsun Hong having excluded” is broken English, and the proposed repair matches the Chinese.
